name: DINKFRAME
headline: From a great shot to a complete customer journey.
summary: A home for a pickleball creative studio, connecting poster orders, client updates and the production workflow.
challenge: A custom creative service needs more than a beautiful storefront. Customers need to share their brief and images, follow progress, review the work and receive their final files.
approach: We brought the public website, customer portal and production workspace into one application. A guided ordering flow collects the right details, while the studio can manage payment review, production stages and delivery in one place.
features: A guided first step
An order journey for creative briefs, player details and image uploads.
A connected workflow
Customer order tracking, review drafts, amendments and final delivery.
A practical studio workspace
An administrative queue, payment review and controlled production updates.
note: A connected product experience covering discovery, ordering, customer updates and studio operations.

name: Phyziolab
headline: Helping people find their next step toward better movement.
summary: A clear, energetic online presence for a sports physiotherapy practice in Ipoh.
challenge: Choosing a physiotherapist starts with trust. People need to understand the approach, explore services and know where to go without wading through confusing language.
approach: We organized the practice around the questions a new visitor brings: who it helps, what care looks like, who is behind it and how to get in touch. Strong typography and purposeful motion give the site a confident, active identity.
features: Clear service information
Treatment options and the practice’s approach presented in an accessible structure.
People behind the practice
Team and movement-focused content help visitors understand the experience.
A direct next step
Location information, directions and a clear contact path for prospective patients.
note: This project showcases the practice’s public website, not a medical records or clinical decision system.

name: The Resthouse
headline: A remarkable place deserves a story you can feel.
summary: An immersive digital introduction to a heritage home on Perhentian Besar.
challenge: The Resthouse is more than a place to stay. Its history, architecture and relationship with the island need space to come through before a visitor thinks about their trip.
approach: We built a flowing editorial experience around the house’s journey, using moving imagery, a historical timeline, architectural details and a browsable gallery. The result gives the destination its own pace and personality online.
features: A cinematic introduction
A full-screen video sets the atmosphere for the island and the house.
A story worth exploring
Heritage, architecture and conservation form a connected narrative.
Details within reach
A visual gallery and visitor information bring the experience closer.
note: An editorial website centered on heritage, conservation and the visitor experience.

name: Ranya Ibrahim Ahmed
headline: A welcoming world for stories, readers and new possibilities.
summary: An author’s creative identity, children’s books and professional services brought together in one place.
challenge: An independent author needs to introduce their work, connect with readers and collaborators, and make it easy to explore and order books.
approach: We paired a warm editorial design with a product catalogue, cart and account experience. The site also gives writing, editing and book development services a clear place alongside the books.
features: An author’s own space
A personal introduction, creative work and professional services in one coherent experience.
Books to browse
Product details and a shopping cart connect discovery to an order journey.
Behind the storefront
Account, order and administration flows support the wider commerce experience.
note: A website and commerce experience for an independent author, with space for books and creative services.

name: PCMS Operations Suite
headline: Software shaped around the way a specialist business works.
summary: A Windows operations suite bringing invoices, certificates, technical reports and verification into one workflow.
challenge: Specialist operations can leave teams moving between documents, emails, records and repeated administrative tasks. Off-the-shelf tools do not always fit the details.
approach: We brought core workflows into a local-first desktop application: consistent documents, structured records, role-aware access and verification. The system also supports reviewed email assistance and controlled software updates.
features: Consistent documentation
Invoices, certificates and technical reports built around the business’s actual workflow.
Connected operational records
Local records, permissions and QR verification support day-to-day use.
Designed for ongoing use
Backups, migrations and controlled updates support the application over time.
note: The visual is a simplified interface illustration. No client records, vessel details or private operational data are shown.

name: Qlynk
headline: Business knowledge, ready for a conversation.
summary: A no-code platform for creating AI agents grounded in approved business knowledge.
challenge: Businesses want useful answers for their customers and teams, with control over what an agent knows, how it responds and where it appears.
approach: Qlynk connects knowledge uploads, agent configuration, hosted pages, website widgets and analytics. Owners can define the agent’s scope and learn where their information needs to improve.
features: Knowledge with a purpose
Approved material, topic boundaries and owner-defined instructions shape the agent.
Where customers need it
Hosted agent pages and embedded website delivery.
A complete product experience
Account management, subscriptions, analytics and knowledge-gap workflows.
note: An independent product in our body of work. Agent behavior depends on its configuration and knowledge sources.

name: DRY Skateboards
headline: A digital identity with a little more attitude.
summary: A skate and streetwear website exploring expressive product presentation and brand storytelling.
challenge: A lifestyle brand needs an online experience with a distinctive point of view, where products and the culture behind them feel connected.
approach: The DRY explorations combine editorial product layouts, motion and Abu Dhabi-inspired campaign storytelling. They demonstrate how a website can express a brand beyond a conventional product grid.
features: Brand-led presentation
A visual direction rooted in skate and streetwear culture.
Products with context
Editorial layouts give merchandise a place within the broader brand story.
Motion with personality
Animated presentation adds energy to the browsing experience.
note: A brand exploration from our wider body of work, focused on digital identity and product storytelling.

name: TapRepute
headline: Making customer feedback easier to give—and more useful.
summary: A customer feedback product connecting QR codes and shared links to a business dashboard.
challenge: Local businesses need a simple way to hear from customers and understand feedback without making the experience long or uncomfortable.
approach: The prototype connects a quick mobile feedback journey to private business insights. Every customer receives the same optional route to Google, regardless of their rating.
features: A simple entry point
Link and QR access let customers reach the mobile feedback flow.
Useful context
Source-aware insights help a business understand where feedback begins.
An equal path for everyone
Optional Google continuation is available for every rating.
note: Validation-stage prototype. Google-link visits are not represented as confirmed public reviews.

name: Aegis Trading Lab
headline: Turning complex data into questions you can test.
summary: A research environment for market data, backtesting, paper trading and risk analysis.
challenge: An idea can look convincing before real-world costs, changing conditions and the quality of the underlying data are considered.
approach: Aegis separates data validation, research, simulation, risk checks and reporting. Its emphasis is on repeatable experiments and evidence that can be inspected, including results that do not support a strategy.
features: Structured research
Validated data and repeatable experiments make the reasoning traceable.
Realistic simulation
Fees, slippage and chronological testing are part of the research process.
Clear boundaries
Paper execution and risk controls keep research separate from live orders.
note: Research and paper-trading software only. No live orders, investment advice or profitability claims.
